### Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)
<a id="l11-hook-template-bank"></a>

Hooks as reusable fill-in templates with blanks ([X], [Y], [niche]) harvested from proven viral reels, each kept with its proof (the example reel and its views). Pick a template, fill the blanks for your niche. A third hook method next to the engineered triple hook (L01) and 'say something crazy' (L08). Adam sells the full bank as a lead magnet: '100+ Proven Viral Hook Templates'.

**How:** Keep a swipe file: template | example reel link | views | niche. Before scripting, fill 3 templates for the idea and pick the strongest; then replace generic words with Srijan's own numbers and self-roast so it passes 'can nobody else say it' (C34).

> 7 hooks that'll always work

## Script

### Triple hook: context, lean, snapback
<a id="hook-triple-hook-formula"></a>

Kallaway-style hook in three steps: context in the first words, a lean that makes the viewer want the next sentence, then a contrarian snapback that yanks them opposite to what they expect (like setting a fishing hook). He calls it the "God-tier hook formula".

> Context, then lean, then snapback is what he calls the "God-tier hook formula".

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L01](../sources/L01.md) · ⚠ [C17](../clashes.md#c17)

### Context in the first words, three channels
<a id="hook-context-first-words"></a>

Say what the video is about immediately, delivered at once by audio, visuals and on-screen text. The creator claims delaying it even to the back half of the first sentence sharply raises skip rate.

**How:** Edits/CapCut: put the topic text on screen from frame 1 while it is said; open on the shot that shows it.

> Deliver the context three ways at once: audio (what you say), visuals (what's on screen) and on-screen text/captions.

### Hook window: 2–3 s short, 15–20 s long
<a id="hook-window-short-vs-long"></a>

Short form gives about 2–3 s to win attention. YouTube long form: about 15–20 s max (the industry says 30 s); the viewer checks it is what they clicked and the right person to hear it from.

> you have about two or three seconds to get their attention

### Expertise hook: years of niche in 60 seconds
<a id="l11-expertise-hook"></a>

Template: "[N years] of [niche] in [60 seconds]". A big time investment, the topic and a tiny time cost in one line: authority without saying 'I'm an expert', plus a compression promise (my years, your minute). Context and lean land together. Reel's example: "3 years of therapy in 60 seconds" (on-screen '3 years of Therapy in 1 minute', pill 40.5M).

**How:** Say it in the first second with the number and the niche as on-screen text. Follow with a fast blitz of the condensed lessons. Use Srijan's real number: "[4] saal ka gym trauma, 60 seconds mein." / "[2,000] hours of Counter-Strike in 60 seconds."

> 3 years of niche in 60 seconds.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C7](../clashes.md#c7)

### Warning hook: never start X without these N things
<a id="l11-warning-hook"></a>

Template: "Never start a [X] if you don't have these [Y] things". A prohibition on a big action the viewer is considering, gated by a counted checklist. Loss aversion plus an open loop (which things? do I have them?); unlike a pure 'don't buy X' debunk it ends with something useful. Reel's example: "Never start a business if you don't have these 4 things" (number tiles 1-2-3-4, red '4 THINGS', pill 339K).

**How:** Pick an action your viewer is about to take (bulk, build a PC, start ranked). Give 3–4 real items, each with a one-line reason; number them on screen with tiles or n/4 badges. "Never build a gaming PC if you don't have these 4 things."

> Never start a business if you don't have these 4 things.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C15](../clashes.md#c15)

### Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see
<a id="l11-desire-hook"></a>

Template: "This is exactly what you want to see when you're [situation]". 'This' points at a visual of the ideal outcome; the situation lets the right viewer self-select. The spoken context arrives at the end of the sentence, so the visual must carry it from frame 1. Reel's example: "This is exactly what you want to see when you're buying an industrial prop[erty]" over an aerial warehouse shot with a map pin (pill 3.6M).

**How:** Open on the proof shot (clean second-hand GPU, FPS counter jumping, shoulder cap in the mirror) and say the line over it; add the situation as text on frame 1 so the context is not late. A snapback line works after it for the funny version.

> This is exactly what you want to see when you're buying an industrial prop[erty].

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C35](../clashes.md#c35)

### Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs
<a id="l11-promise-hook"></a>

Template: "If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]". A tiny repeatable habit, 'every single day', then three concrete outcomes (rule of three). Each outcome is another reason to care. Reel's example: "If you take creatine every single day, you're going to build more muscle, recover faster, and get way more out of all the hard work that you're putting in in the gym" (pill 28M, the reel's biggest example).

**How:** Keep each payoff concrete and true (no invented percentages). Make the third payoff the funny one for Srijan: "…aur Sunday ki biryani guilt-free ho jaayegi." Pop the three payoffs as text one by one.

> If you take B every single day, you're going to X, Y, and Z.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: gym, tech, gaming, all · stated · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C7](../clashes.md#c7)

### Challenge, ranking and list templates
<a id="l11-classic-hook-templates"></a>

The three classic templates spelled out: Challenge "I'm going to [X] for [Y] days straight" (example: study 8 hours, 5 days straight, 4.9M); Ranking "Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]" (example: rating supplements so you don't waste your money, S–F tier board, 4.7M); List "These are the 5 best ways to use [X]" (example: sound effects, 1.9M). Each carries a hard number or names what the viewer saves.

**How:** Challenge: "Main 30 din roz 100 push-ups karunga." Ranking: "Rating every ₹1,500 gaming mouse so you don't waste your salary." List: "5 best ways to use your purana laptop." Use a day counter, tier board or n/5 badges.

> Rating X so you don't waste your Y.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches: all · stated · from [L11](../sources/L11.md) · ⚠ [C3](../clashes.md#c3) ⚠ [C20](../clashes.md#c20)

## Graphics

### Visual table of contents in the first 2 s
<a id="l11-toc-intro"></a>

0–2 s: a blur-in and a 30% eased punch-out while a frosted-glass numbered list of all 7 hook names scrolls up above his head and '7HOOK' (heavy rounded red neon sans + white script 'that'll always work') sits on his chest. The viewer sees the whole menu (and the count) before the first item.

**How:** For list reels, flash the numbered menu of items in the first 1–2 s (glass cards scrolling up) under the spoken title; it is the visual form of a promised-list open loop.

> 7 hooks that'll always work
